task.title: Troubleshoot database and storage issues
task.shortdesc: Diagnose local SQLite, storage path, backup, and profile visibility issues without editing database rows directly.

prereq.p: Use this procedure when profiles disappear, writes fail, migration evidence is unclear, backup checksums do not match, or BPM_DATABASE_URL points to an unexpected location.

context.p: Current source deployment uses local storage such as sqlite+aiosqlite:///./data/bpm.db and repository-owned files under data/, schema cache paths, and documentation site paths. There is no managed backup or restore orchestration in BPM 0.9.0.

step.cmd: Confirm the active database URL and working directory.

info.p: Record BPM_DATABASE_URL, current directory, source revision, and whether the process runs from Linux filesystem or /mnt/c. Do not assume two shells point at the same data/bpm.db.

step.cmd: Check migration and profile API evidence before opening storage files.

info.p: Focused rerun: alembic upgrade head, then curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/profiles?limit=50. If the API returns expected profiles, the symptom may be filter, lifecycle, or browser state.

step.cmd: Verify backup evidence before destructive recovery.

info.p: Check mkdir -p backups, cp data/bpm.db backups/bpm-pre-update.db, and sha256sum backups/bpm-pre-update.db records. Keep exports of critical policies.json profiles as separate evidence.
Do not edit SQLite rows, generated artifacts, or schema cache files as routine recovery. Use documented profile archive, restore, import, export, or update-from-source procedures instead.

step.cmd: Escalate with storage evidence when recovery is unsafe.

info.p: Include database URL, file path, checksum, migration command, API response, and backup/export evidence.
info.note: If no verified pre-failure backup exists, stop before deleting or replacing data/bpm.db; BPM does not provide point-in-time recovery.

result.p: The operator has a storage diagnosis that preserves user data and separates database state from UI or filter symptoms.

postreq.p: After storage is stable, rerun health/readiness and the smallest affected API workflow.
